prompt.text: Which of the following spans the entire phospholipid bilayer (with regions exposed on both sides of the membrane)?

questions.explanation: Integral (transmembrane) proteins span the bilayer with surfaces exposed on both sides.

prompt.text: True or false: Plant cell membranes can contain sterols that function similarly to cholesterol.

questions.explanation: Plant membranes often contain phytosterols and related sterols that help regulate fluidity, similar to cholesterol in animal cells.

prompt.text: As a replacement for cholesterol, plant cells often use _____ to achieve a similar function:

questions.explanation: Plants often use other steroid lipids/phytosterols in place of animal cholesterol to modulate fluidity.

prompt.text: Plants and animals that live in cold environments have ___ points of unsaturation in their lipid bilayers

questions.explanation: More unsaturation keeps membranes fluid at low temperature by preventing tight packing.

prompt.text: The following are all functions of peripheral proteins, except:

questions.explanation: Peripheral proteins aid shape, signaling, and enzymes; transport across the bilayer is typically integral proteins’ role.

prompt.text: Proteins with short carbohydrate tags are known as:

questions.explanation: Glycoproteins are proteins with covalently attached carbohydrate chains.

prompt.text: Which molecules do not require transport proteins to aid their diffusion across the cell membrane?

questions.explanation: Lipid-soluble (nonpolar) molecules can diffuse through the hydrophobic core without transporters.
Facilitated diffusion is still passive (no energy input), but it requires a channel or carrier protein.

options: Volume of water to be equal across a membrane
Concentration of solute to be equal across a membrane
Concentration of solvent to be equal across a membrane
questions.answer: Concentration of solute to be equal across a membrane
questions.explanation: Osmotic equilibrium is reached when solute concentrations (effective osmolarity) are equal across the membrane.

prompt.text: Complete the sentence about normal tonicity for plant and animal cells.

sentence: Relative to their surroundings under normal conditions, a plant cell is
questions.explanation: Plant cells are typically hypertonic to their surroundings (water enters; turgid), while animal cells are usually isotonic with their extracellular fluid.

prompt.text: True or false: Energy for active transport does not always come directly from ATP.

questions.explanation: Active transport can be powered directly by ATP or indirectly by energy stored in gradients (secondary active transport / cotransport).

prompt.text: When active and passive transport are coupled, it is known as:

questions.explanation: Cotransport couples the downhill movement of one solute to uphill movement of another.

prompt.text: True or false: Chemical gradients and electrochemical gradients can work in opposite directions.

questions.explanation: Chemical and electrical components of the electrochemical gradient can favor movement in opposite directions.

prompt.text: Receptor-mediated endocytosis is a form of:

questions.explanation: Receptor-mediated endocytosis is a specialized form of pinocytosis that takes in specific ligands.
